METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS [
COLD FILTER PLUGGlNG UDC

P : 110 ]
POINT OF DISTILLATE : 536.421~4 FUELS

Adapted, with permission from the Institute of Petroleum Method Designation IP 309/80 1. SCOPE 1.1 This method describes a procedure for the determination of the low temperature operability of distillate fuels ( automotive diesel fuels and gas oils ), including those containing a flow improving additive. 1.2 This test may not be applicable to the determination of the low temperature operability of distillate fuels used in equipment with exposed paper filters in the fuel supply system, 2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 2.1 The fuel sample is cooled under the prescribed conditions and, at intervals of l"C, a vacuum of 200 mm water gauge is applied to draw the fuel As the fuel cools below its cloud point, through a fine iyire mesh filter. increasing amounts of wax crystals will be formed. These will cause the flow rate to decrease and eventually complete plugging of the filter will occur. 3. TERMINOLOGY 3.1 The Cold Filter Pluggilmg Point - It is defined as the highest temperature ( expressed as a multiple of 1�C ) at which the fuel, when cooled under the prescribed conditions, either will not flow through the filter or requires more than 60 seconds for 20 ml to pass through. 4. APPARATUS 4.0 The apparatus required for this test is illustrated in Fig. 1 and 2 and consist of the following. @ Copyright 1982

4.1 Test Jar - A cylindrical test jar of clear glass, flat bottom, with internal diameter 31'0 to 32-O mm, a wall thickness of l*O to l-5 mm, and a height of 115 to 125 mm. The jar shall have an etched mark at the 45 ml level. 4.2 Jacket - A water-tight cylindrical the dimensions given in Fig. 2. jacket of brass, flat bottom, with

4.3 Supporting Ring - An adaptor of oil resistant plastic is required to position the jar and the jacket respectively in relation to the jacket and the cooling bath. A suitable form is shown in Fig. 2. This design may, however, be modified to suit existing cooling baths. 4.4 Insulating Ring and Spacer ( see Fig. 2 ) - Made from oil resistant plastic and used to insulate the test jar from the bottom and sides of the jacket. The spacer shall fit closely to the test jar and loosely inside the jacket. 3

4.6.1 A pointer and spring wire clip are used to position meter correctly and maintain it in that position.

4.7 Pipette with Filter Unit - The pipette made from clear glass is connected to the filter unit ( see Fig. 2 ) using a screwed cap with O-rings and brass spacers. 4.7.1 The wire mesh holder for the test gauze is shown in Fig. 2. The fine wire mesh has a nominal aperture width of 45 micrometres. The mesh is firmly clamped in position by a retaining ring which is pressed on to the mesh holder. 4.7.2 The filter unit is made from brass and the mesh from stainless steel. The O-ring material is oil resistant plastic.
*Thermometer with the Institute of Petroleum designation 1P IC conforms requirements. Thermometers with designation IP 2C may also be used. to these

IS : 1448 [ P : 110 ] - 1981 4.8 Cooling Bath - The type of cooling bath is optional, but shall be of a shape and size suitable for supporting the jacket at the required depth. Maintain the bath temperature at the required value by a refrigeration A cooling bath as used unit or by the use of suitable freezing mixtures. in IS : 1448 ( P : 10 )-1970* may be suitable. For determinations of cold filter plugging points below -20�C a second ( and possibly a third ) bath If several testing units are placed in one large cooling will be required. bath the distance between the jacket walls shall be at least 50 mm. 4.9 Vacuum Source - A large glass bottle, partly filled with water and The connected to a vacuum pump, acts as constant vacuum reservoir. constant vacuum is maintained at 200 mm water gauge by ensuring a continuous air bleed of 3 to 4 litres/h into the reservoir. This is illustrated in Fig. 1 which shows the layout of the test apparatus. 4.10 Stop Watch Graduated to O-2 seconds.

5. PREPARATION

OF SAMPLE

5.1 Filter the sample to be tested through dry lintless filter paper, making the filtration at a temperature of 15�C or higher. 6. PREPARATION OF FILTER

6.1 Before each test, dismantle the filter unit and wash the pieces as well as the test jar and thermometer with a low boiling solvent such as 60/ 80 petroleuin ether or l,l,l-trichloroethane, using the vacuum to suck solvent into the pipette above the etched mark. Rinse with acetone and dry in an air stream. 6.2 Examine the wire mesh and O-rings for contamination or damage and, Assemble the parts as shown in Fig. 1. Ensure that if necessary, renew. the assembly is clean and dry before inserting into the next jar of test fuel. 7. PROCEDURE 7.1 Dry the insulating ring and spacer and place on the bottom previously dried jacket. of the

7.2 Pour the filtered sample into the test jar to the etched mark ( 45 ml ). Wipe the test jar to ensure that the outside is clean and dry.
*Methods of test for petroleum and its products: P 10 Cloud point and pour point.

6

1s :

1448.fP : 110 J -1981

7.3 Close the test jar with the stopper carrying the pipette, filter unit and thermometer. Ensure that the bulb of the thermometer is not in contact with the side of the test jar of the filter body. Only use a low range thermometer if the expected cold filter plugging point is below -30�C. Thermometers shall not be changed during the test. 7.4 Insert filter unit positioned end is 1.3 the test jar rests on by the use to 1.7 mm assembly in a vertical position into the jacket. The the bottom of the test jar and the thermometer is of the pointer and spring wire clip so that its lower above the bottom of the test jar.

7.5 If the jacket is not an integral part of the cooling bath, place the jacket containing the test jar assembly vertically to a depth of 83 to 87 mm into the cooling bath which is maintained at a temperature of -34 &0.5%. 7.6 Connect the top of the pipette to the vacuum system by means of flexible tubing. Testing may be commenced immediately but if the cloud point of the sample is known it may be preferable to delay testing until the sample has cooled to a temperature of not less than 5�C above its cloud However, testing shall start while the sample is still in the -34 & point. 0.5% bath. 7.7 If the sample reaches a temperature of -20% before the cold filter plugging point is reached, quickly transfer the test jar to a jacket in a cooling bath maintained at - 51 f 0*5"C. If the sample has not reached its cold filter plugging point when its temperature reaches -35�C quickly transfer the test jar to a jacket in a bath maintained at - 67 f 2�C. 7.8 Conimence testing at a sample temperature which is a multiple of 1�C by turning the three-way tap so that the filter assembly is connected to the vacuum system, causing the sample to be drawn through the fine wire Once the sample has reached the etched mark on mesh into the pipette. the pipette, turn the three-way tap to its initial position to ventrthe pipette and so allow the sample to return to the test jar. 7.9 Repeat the operation described in 7.8 at 1�C intervals until the temperature is reached at which either the sample ceases to flow through the filter or the pipette is not filled to the etched mark within 60 seconds. Record the temperature at which this last filtration commenced.
NOTE - Occasionally, when a sample has cooled almost to its cold filter plugging point, it will fill the pipette to the etched mark when tested but will not flow back into the test jar when the pipette is vented. If this happens, the sample shall be considered to have plugged the filter and the temperature shall be recorded as above.

8. REPORT 8.1 Report the temperature Point. recorded in 7.9 as the Cold Filter Plugging
